title: PRD: Session Credit Forecasting & Simulation API
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This PRD describes the Session Credit Forecasting & Simulation API: a developer-facing service and SDK that predicts per-session credit consumption, simulates billing outcomes for candidate routing/quantization choices, and provides a local SDK for offline cost forecasting during developer onboarding. The feature is targeted at self-serve customers and platform teams who need deterministic previews of billing impact before making routing, fidelity, or warm-capacity decisions.

Why this matters
- Customers repeatedly ask for fast, explainable cost forecasts tied to session semantics (session length, streaming duration, kv-cache reuse).
- Sales and SREs run manual simulations today; automating this reduces onboarding friction and dispute volume.
- Tighter forecasting enables better pricing experiments (microbundles, per-minute credits) and reduces surprise overages.

Goals (success criteria)
- API returns a predictive credit estimate within 200ms for standard queries and within 95th percentile error <= 10% on sampled tenant traffic within 8 weeks of rollout.
- SDK provides reproducible local simulations that match production-calculated credits within 5% for deterministic workloads.
- Integrated into Console Cost Explorer: customers can run scenario simulations and save up to 3 candidate plans per account.
- Reduce first-line billing disputes related to session charge expectations by 60% in the first 3 months after launch.

Non-goals
- This PRD does not change billing semantics or contract definitions. The API is advisory; legal/contracting changes are out of scope.
- We will not support streaming micro-billing (per-frame microcredits) at v1.

High-level user stories
1) Developer (self-serve): "I want to estimate monthly credits used by my chatbot given average turn length=40 tokens, 500 monthly active sessions, and 20% long-running sessions".
2) Platform engineer: "Simulate the impact of enabling 4-bit quantization and switching from model-a to model-b on peak credit usage for our integration tests."
3) Account manager: "Create three pricing scenarios for customer ACME and export a CSV to include in the onboarding proposal."

Functional requirements
- FR-1: PredictiveEstimator endpoint: POST /api/v1/forecast with structured payload (session_profile, model_variants, routing_policy, kv_cache_hit_rate, batching_profile, duration_distribution). Returns: median_estimate, p10, p90, estimated_compute_ms, token_breakdown.
- FR-2: SimulationRunner endpoint: POST /api/v1/simulate accepts a traffic_trace (ndjson or zipped traces) and returns per-session credit traces plus aggregate billing projections for configurable time windows (hour/day/month).
- FR-3: Local SDK (Python + Node): exposes simulate_forecast(...) that runs the same deterministic estimator logic locally with a shippable model of kernels/latency and cost coefficients. SDK must include a locked coefficient file (versioned) and a validation mode to compare SDK vs production.
- FR-4: Console integration: embed an interactive simulator in Console > Cost Explorer with a Save Scenario button and CSV export.
- FR-5: Explainability: API must return a breakdown of cost contributors (tokens_generated, kv-cache_misses, batch_overhead, warmup_amortization) and a short human-readable rationale string.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1: 95th percentile latency for Forecast endpoint <= 200ms.
- NFR-2: Forecast endpoint throughput: 1000 qps per region at launch.
- NFR-3: Accuracy: median absolute percent error <= 10% on production A/B sample for specified tenant classes.
- NFR-4: SDK reproducibility: deterministic mode yields identical estimates to production within 5% for recorded traces.
- NFR-5: Data retention: trace uploads for SimulationRunner retained for 30 days, encrypted at rest (KMS).

API: canonical examples
- POST /api/v1/forecast (JSON body)
  {
    "session_profile": {"avg_turn_tokens": 38, "avg_turns_per_session": 6, "streamed": true, "avg_stream_seconds": 2.4},
    "model_variants": ["rwd-3b-q4f32", "rwd-7b-q4f16"],
    "routing_policy": "latency_prefer_cheap_fallback",
    "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.65,
    "batching_profile": {"avg_batch_size": 8, "max_batch_latency_ms": 30}
  }
- Response (truncated):
  {
    "median_estimate_credits": 1234,
    "p10": 980,
    "p90": 1450,
    "token_breakdown": {"input_tokens": 1200000, "output_tokens": 800000},
    "explain": "Most cost driven by output tokens and 35% batch overhead on short sessions."
  }

Simulation CLI example
- rwd-sim run --trace ./sample-trace.ndjson --scenario "quant4-enable" --out ./sim-results.csv

Telemetry & metrics (required)
- Event keys: forecast.request, forecast.latency_ms, forecast.error_margin, simulate.batch_size, sdk.local_validation_pass, console.scenario_saved.
- Metrics: forecast_p50_latency_ms, forecast_p95_latency_ms, forecast_accuracy_mape (mean absolute percent error), simulate_avg_runtime_ms.
- Logs: include trace_id, tenant_id (hashed if external), estimator_version, feature_flags at time of call.

SLOs & thresholds
- Forecast endpoint p95 latency <= 200ms (SLO). Error budget 0.5% monthly.
- SimulationRunner p99 runtime <= 60s for trace files <= 10k sessions.
- SDK local validation mismatch rate <= 5% (compared across validation traces).

Security, privacy & compliance
- Accept only authenticated uploads. SimulationRunner must require owner-level role or an explicit signed upload token.
- Do not store PII in trace uploads. Provide a trace sanitizer CLI (rwd-sim sanitize) to remove user text with regex redaction.
- All stored traces encrypted with customer-owned KMS option for Private deployments.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Lab alpha (2 weeks) — internal teams + SEs. Collect baseline accuracy on 5 synthetic apps.
2) Limited beta (6 weeks) — invited customers (20 tenants) + Console integration behind feature flag. Monitor forecast_accuracy_mape and billing disputes.
3) Public launch (GA, 2 months after beta) — wide availability for Hosted + Dedicated. SDK published to PyPI/NPM.
4) Post-launch (quarterly) — extend to per-minute streaming microbilling, add per-route pricing presets.

Migration and customer comms
- Provide an onboarding checklist: how to sample traces, recommended session profiles for common patterns (chatbot, assistant, summarizer).
- Offer a 1-hour joint workshop with SE for top 10 onboarding customers.
- Update pricing FAQ to clarify advisory nature and not a contract amendment.

Analytics & validation plan
- A/B validation: route 10% of forecast traffic to ground-truth billing reconciler and compute forecast_accuracy_mape weekly.
- KPIs to track: reduction in billing disputes, time-to-onboard, scenario saves per tenant, SDK downloads.

Ownership
- Product owner: Priya Patel (product)
- Engineering: Forecasting Service team (eng-serving-runtime), lead: Jonas Richter
- SDK: Developer Experience (eng-developer-experience), lead: Maya Chen
- GTM & SE kit: Customer Success & Sales Engineering, lead: Ethan Brooks

Dependencies
- Billing metering API (billing-service v2) — required for reconciliation 1:1.
- Telemetry pipeline (telemetry-v3) for forecast metrics.
- Console Cost Explorer embedding work (console-web-3).

Open questions
1) Should the API expose model-specific kernel coefficients or keep them internal?
2) What retention policy do legal/regulatory teams require for trace samples beyond 30 days?
3) Pricing: do we bill heavy SimulationRunner usage to tenants? Propose free tier + paid heavy-runner SKU.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Forecasts are wrong for edge-case multimodal sessions. Mitigation: add conservative uncertainty bands (p10/p90) and label those scenarios in Console.
- Risk: Customers interpret forecast as contractual. Mitigation: explicit disclaimer in responses and Console UIs; legal review of wording.

Acceptance criteria (for GA)
- FR-1..FR-5 implemented and covered by e2e tests.
- Forecast accuracy MAPE <= 10% on benchmark tenants.
- 95th percentile latency < 200ms in production load tests.
- SDK release with CI validation mode and sample trace generator.

Appendices
- Sample session profiles (JSON) for common use cases: conversational chat, long-running stream, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
- Validation harness commands and reference datasets (internal).
